summary.race_pattern: Five climb-plus-descent loops plus an exit climb lap.

coaching_rules: Use 2024-11-03 as the main Bukit Kiara enduro race benchmark for rebuilding race-repeat fitness.
Clayton believes current DH pace potential is faster than this benchmark, but current fitness is below benchmark level.
The primary rebuild gap is sustained climb speed, between-stage recovery, and ability to repeat hard descents after repeated climbs.

Progress Kiara durability from 3 quality loops to 4 and then 5 before simulating full race stress.

uplift_or_shuttle_dh_run.interpretation: Use descent count, braking quality, grip confidence, upper-body fatigue, and risk exposure as the main limits; Garmin load can understate impact cost when uplift removes climbing.

self_pedaled_enduro_trail_day.interpretation: Treat as a real enduro durability day, not just DH skill. Climbing load, heat, repeated descents, braking fatigue, and late-run skill quality all matter.

setup_feedback.rider_feedback: Zeb setup was good with a bit of arm pump on descents.
setup_feedback.next_adjustment_to_test: Try 1 click more rebound damping and 1 click less low-speed compression damping at the next Bukit Dinding session.

specialized_enduro.power_meter_preference: Do not move the power meter here by default; Clayton prefers to ride the Enduro bike on feel.

clipless_adaptation.athlete_response: Clipless felt natural on the Enduro and possibly slightly more comfortable than flat pedals.
clipless_adaptation.comparison_context: The prior 2026-06-12 Enduro exposure used flat pedals; the 2026-08-08 re-entry followed a 57-day Enduro-specific gap while clipless skill had been developed on the Stumpjumper.
clipless_adaptation.coaching_interpretation: The primary adaptation is transfer of clipless automaticity and dynamically centred rider behavior from the Stumpjumper to the Enduro. Foot security is a secondary enabler of front-tyre authority and bike-body separation, not evidence that the pedals alone created the technical improvement.
clipless_adaptation.validation_constraint: Keep the pedal system fixed during the next matched Enduro repeat. Retain clipless as successful Enduro transfer only while release remains automatic, knee and hip response stay clean, centred posture and front tracking persist, and the rider does not rely on pulling against the pedals to correct the bike.

specialized_stumpjumper.default_role: Outdoor trail bike with current power meter.
specialized_stumpjumper.preferred_training_use: Power-meter climb-focused Bukit Kiara loop sessions: focus the workout on repeated climbs and cruise the same descent trail to control risk and isolate aerobic/torque fitness.
specialized_stumpjumper.mileage_policy: Clayton is comfortable putting training mileage on the Stumpjumper.
specialized_stumpjumper.trainer_swap_option: Can replace the Marin SQ3 on the Elite Suito if needed.

setup_history.change: Fork rebound damping increased by one click and shock rebound damping reduced by one click.
setup_history.rider_rationale: The fork rebound increase addressed front-wheel ping over big hits that had pushed Clayton rearward; treat the slower rebound as a previously successful correction rather than an untested cause.

setup_history.change: Fork HSC one click firmer than the 2026-07-28 setting.
setup_history.positive_context: Clayton previously loved this setting at maximum attack on 2K+ through successive hits.
setup_history.negative_context: During a separate illness-fatigue period Clayton could not ride the firmer setting effectively and returned HSC one click softer.
setup_history.interpretation: Treat HSC as a provisional intent- and readiness-dependent setting: firmer attack support when fresh versus the softer compliance setting for genuinely chill riding. Validate rather than assuming either setting is universally superior.

setup_history.change: Tested the fork one click firmer in HSC than the 2026-07-28 setting while retaining the previously successful slower rebound direction.
setup_history.rider_outcome: Clayton reported a stronger dynamically centred posture, greater willingness to load the front, no leftward veer, no perceived rear wallow, more controlled corner exits, and remaining chassis headroom.
setup_history.objective_context: At the 1,118.38 m distance-synchronised overlap, the 2K lap was 11.768 seconds (5.5 percent) faster than 2026-07-25 and 7.551 seconds (3.6 percent) faster than 2026-07-28, with no lap-comparator quality flags. Power was also higher, so this is not a setup-only gain. Pure Quill was shortened by a missed exit and did not reproduce the prior 38 km/h maximum-speed condition.
setup_history.interpretation: Retain HSC +1 provisionally as the attack setting. The primary gain is improved rider centring and front-pressure authority; the firmer HSC is a credible secondary enabler by holding the front higher under larger impacts. Do not credit the result to setup alone and do not add another click.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Re-test HSC +1 on an exact familiar route at 85-90 percent with no other setup changes. Keep it only if the fork recovers between successive hits without ping, pack-down, harsh deflection, left pull, rearward hip retreat, rear wallow, kick, chassis pitch, loss of small-hit grip, or increased hand and braking fatigue.

setup_history.change: Promoted fork HSC +1 relative to the 2026-07-28 setting from provisional attack setting to the working Stumpjumper baseline for normal-readiness, familiar Bukit Kiara riding.
setup_history.rider_outcome: In a chill-pace within-ride HSC +1 / HSC -1 / HSC +1 sequence, Clayton reported that +1 felt harsher but retained greater exit commitment; -1 produced more mid-turn braking and reduced commitment to the exit. Returning to +1 on a partial final 2K confirmed the preferred control direction before focus declined.
setup_history.interpretation: The primary adaptation remains Clayton's dynamically centred posture, deliberate front loading and rapid recentering. HSC +1 is a secondary enabler that plausibly preserves chassis support so that rider skill can be expressed. HSC responds to damper shaft speed rather than trail speed, so a harsher feel at slower pace is acceptable only while tyre tracking, grip and hand/upper-body fatigue remain clean. Do not add another click or use HSC -1 as a workaround for declining focus.
setup_history.scope: Working baseline only for normal-readiness, familiar Kiara terrain. Wet roots, long rough descents, unfamiliar terrain and impaired or compromised CNS readiness remain unvalidated; impaired or compromised CNS status blocks technical testing rather than selecting a softer setting to continue.
setup_history.validation_constraint: Hold tyre pressures, fork air/sag, rebound, shock and other setup variables constant. Falsify HSC +1 if matched runs show front ping, skip, harsh lateral deflection, reduced root or small-hit grip, travel starvation, pack-down, rear kick, chassis pitch, rearward hip retreat, left pull, reactive braking, missed exits or greater hand, braking or upper-body fatigue.

power_meter_policy.default: Keep the Stumpjumper power meter available for outdoor power validation and selected structured MTB data.
power_meter_policy.enduro_bike: Use feel, RPE, HR, repeat quality, and trail notes rather than power as the primary guide.
power_meter_policy.indoor_bike: Use the Elite Suito as the main controlled indoor power source; compare with the Stumpjumper power meter only when calibration or transfer questions matter.
power_meter_policy.marin_sq3: Move the power meter to the Marin SQ3 only if outdoor hardtail power data becomes strategically useful, not for routine indoor trainer work.

calibration_notes.note: Elite Suito appears accurate up to about 200 W; above that it under-reads by about 10% based on power meter 300 W versus Suito 270 W.
calibration_notes.coaching_use: Use Suito power normally for endurance/tempo under about 200 W. For high-power indoor targets above 200 W, account for under-reading or validate against the bike power meter before using the result for FTP or anaerobic conclusions.

garmin_hrm_strap.audit_rule: If a mountain bike activity has no external HEART_RATE sensor in Devices & Apps, treat HR and Garmin load as lower confidence.

rider_category.experienced_definition: Carries speed through most corners found on trail, including rough, banked, and flat corners. Larger jumps and drops are hit frequently and with precision. Rides hard trails with consistent comfort, confidence, and precision.
rider_category.expert_definition: Upper echelon aggressive trail skill: scrubbing jumps, heavy flat landings at pace, aggressive technical terrain, repeatable speed into and out of challenging corners, and comfort with wheel slides.

work.domain: Building an AI workflow for NYSE and Nasdaq trading.
work.cognitive_demand: High: sustained analysis, workflow design, and trading-related decision work.
work.timing: Work often extends late into the Kuala Lumpur evening and may cross midnight.
work.unknowns_rule: Do not invent a work cutoff or assume the demanding workday is complete from low morning Garmin stress; collect actual start/end timing.

training_placement.preferred_rule: Train after the main sleep period and before the late U.S.-market work window; do not place hard training after work finishes in the early morning.
training_placement.current_observed_pattern: Recent MTB sessions are usually late morning to early afternoon, while indoor bike sessions commonly begin in the late afternoon before the market-work window.
training_placement.key_mtb_rule: Place consequence-bearing MTB after the best available sleep opportunity and a fresh mental-clarity check, not merely a green Body Battery.
training_placement.minimum_viable_busy_week: One controlled Suito bike touch plus one MTB exposure; preserve Sunday Sabbath and avoid replacing missed bike work with hard non-bike load.

segmented_sleep.principle: A planned nap or morning sleep extension may support a late-market schedule, but it supplements rather than erases short primary sleep or accumulated sleep debt.
segmented_sleep.garmin_limitation: Current Garmin data reports zero nap time and cannot be trusted to confirm that no nap occurred; actual nap timing, duration, inertia, and post-nap clarity require structured athlete input.
segmented_sleep.validation_window: Use a 2-3 week prospective log before promoting segmented sleep as a proven Clayton-specific recovery strategy.

wearable_context.usual_wear_pattern: Worn continuously day and night except for dress-watch substitution, normal showers, charging, or other explicitly reported removal; at home the strap may sometimes be loosened enough to interrupt optical HR while the watch remains worn.

optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.athlete_confirmed_rule: The stop and restart of Fenix wrist-HR readings define the observed optical-HR measurement-unavailable boundary at the device sample-transition resolution.
optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.physical_wear_state_rule: A wrist-HR gap does not by itself prove that the watch was removed because a loosened strap can produce the same signal loss.
optical_hr_measurement_interpretation.cause_rule: Do not assign dress-watch substitution, loose strap, shower, charging, or another cause to an individual gap without exact target-date athlete confirmation.

reported_recurring_exceptions.label: Sunday church dress-watch substitution
reported_recurring_exceptions.occurrence_rule: This recurring habit is context only. Do not instantiate or time a dated off-wrist interval without athlete-confirmed start and end times.

interpretation_rules: Intentional off-wrist time is coverage provenance, not physiological recovery evidence.
Missing or negative-sentinel samples never prove off-wrist status by themselves.
A direct target-date wrist-HR gap confirms optical-HR measurement unavailability at sample-transition resolution but does not prove physical watch removal or identify its cause.
Keep measurement availability, physical wear state, and cause attribution as separate fields.
Attribute each material unavailable run only where a strict target-date athlete-confirmed interval overlaps it; recurring context and unmatched remainders stay unexplained.
Positive low-stress use requires dense valid target-date samples from near midnight through a declared cutoff at or after 18:00, credible Garmin cadence, and no uncovered tail.
Fresh target-date wear coverage supersedes cached same-day model predictions that depended on low stress; mask them until rebuilt.
Never impute stress, Body Battery, sleep, HRV, steps, or readiness across an off-wrist interval.
Material internal unavailability withholds positive low-stress credit; high observed stress may still downshift the call.

Protect 2 MTB exposures per week: one quality/skill day and one durability/enduro-volume day.
Use current Garmin FTP plus RPE/HR response for one structured engine session when density supports it; keep the remaining indoor bike touches low aerobic.
Use elliptical as recovery/support only, not as the aerobic backbone of a bike-performance block.

individual_adaptation_profile.core_finding: Clayton responds best to bike-specific continuity. Total load alone is misleading because elliptical/run/gym can keep load high while cycling power and cycling VO2 fall.
individual_adaptation_profile.detraining_pattern: Fitness dropped when bike-specific load/frequency fell from 2025-12 through 2026-04, despite high elliptical/non-bike load.
individual_adaptation_profile.elliptical_role: Useful for recovery and aerobic continuity, especially HR-capped, but it must not replace weekly bike touches during MTB-performance blocks.
individual_adaptation_profile.gym_role: Useful as a small durability support dose only if it does not reduce Friday/Saturday trail quality or create DOMS before key rides.

maintenance_floor.notes: The issue is multi-week bike droughts, not Sabbath or normal recovery.
maintenance_floor.counting_rule: Count unique bike days, not split activity files or doubles created only to manufacture frequency.

cns_readiness_policy.decision_role: Use CNS readiness as the technical-consequence ceiling after Sabbath and physical readiness.
cns_readiness_policy.why_it_exists: Clayton can show low or manageable training load while still having brain fog, low HRV, weak feel, slow processing, or reduced braking/line-choice precision after systemic stress, heat, illness, or dense technical riding.
cns_readiness_policy.green_signal: Mental clarity, normal vision width, fast line choice, deliberate braking release, no unclipping delay, strong/normal feel for the dose, and stable HRV/stress context.
cns_readiness_policy.yellow_signal: Motivated and physically capable, but with residual brain fog, weak feel, low HRV, elevated stress, or uncertainty about decision speed.
cns_readiness_policy.red_signal: Brain fog, sick/systemic stress, strained HRV, weak or very weak feel at low RPE, delayed processing, or confidence masking sloppy timing.
cns_readiness_policy.if_watch: Use one familiar skill target, low-to-moderate consequence, no speed hunting, no stacked setup changes, and stop when decision speed drops.
cns_readiness_policy.if_compromised_or_impaired: No speed, jumps, enduro simulation, high-consequence descending, setup testing, hard intervals, or heavy gym loading; use rest, recovery, or low-consequence repetition only.
subjective_notes_required: braking timing compared with first descent
whether the final descent decision speed matched the first

operating_model.coach_role: interpret evidence, resolve conflicts, and make the final coaching call
operating_model.nutrition_role: fuel training, recovery, body composition, and adaptation
operating_model.predictive_loop: Before training, store the expected session load/RPE, raw next-day response, coaching-adjusted strain response, execution-drift stress test, and schema v3 contract. After Garmin sync, compare action alignment, actual load, self-evaluation, technical outcome, explicit stop-rule outcome, review-field completion, and next-day response against the stored expectation. Keep physiology-only matches visible, but only complete contract-quality sessions calibrate the model; drifted or incomplete sessions update execution-risk and evidence-quality rules first.
operating_model.software_role: stage evidence, normalize data, apply repeatable safety rules

bike_specific_continuity.downshift_warning: Do not allow high elliptical/non-bike load to hide a bike-specific drought.
bike_specific_continuity.counting_rule: Count unique bike days, not split activity files. Any hard run counts toward the meaningful-cost cap.

elliptical_use.allowed: Recovery/support aerobic work, usually HR-capped around 120 bpm.
elliptical_use.not_allowed: Backbone modality during a bike-performance block unless trail access or logistics require it.

heart_rate_source_confidence.rule: When Devices & Apps does not show an external HEART_RATE sensor on MTB, treat wrist-HR-derived load, zones, and intensity as lower confidence.
heart_rate_source_confidence.wrist_hr_limitation: Fenix wrist optical HR may under-read during technical MTB because grip pressure, vibration, sweat, and arm pump reduce optical signal quality.

cns_readiness.rule: When CNS readiness is impaired or compromised, remove technical consequence and high intensity even if load is low or Body Battery has rebounded.

strength_training.default_dose: 1-2 short support sessions per week, 20-35 min.
strength_training.interference_rule: If gym compromises Friday/Saturday trail quality, reduce volume, load, or placement.
